The morning after that long night and glorious crank that got the motorcycle engine running again. Alp is back and now it is time to apply the last touches to the bike to get her back and running on the road again. Today is the last day down south. Plenty to do still. Fill the brake system with brake fluid to get some stopping power for the motorbike. Prepara the Africa Twin fuel tank with taps, sensor and plug to go on the motorcycle without leaks. Run into a problem there with the left hand fuel tap bumping into one of the engine coolant pipes which is seriously in the way. Put the wheels back on. Receive the Hammerite paint for the suspension linkage but too late. Also finally receive the Fuelflow piston fuel pump which is going onto the bike at a later stage. Because part of the bigger XRV750 fuel tank sits below the carburetors, gravity won't suffice for the last few liters of fuel. A low PSI fuel pump is needed. Getting real close to departure now! Also get a better listen of the new Delkevic 350mm exhaust.

-

My name is Pedro Mota and I ride my trusty Honda Transalp motorcycle around the world. Me and Alp have been on the road now for over two years and have ridden through at least thirty countries. This motorcycle adventure has taken us through Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia, Russia, East Asia and Australia. Meet great people, see extraordinary places. Join me on this motorbike ride around the world and experience life on the road. A man and his motorcycle living the dream. Because life there is only one.
author: Pedro Mota
